text:
carla: quick heads-up — during onboarding of the new int4 model build (redwood/llama-7b-int4-v2) i'm seeing token divergence only after ~6500 tokens when kvcache eviction starts. seems deterministic for our long-doc test corpus :eyes:
noah: ugh. any chance it's a rope scaling issue vs a kv index misalign? can you paste the minimal repro?
carla: here's what i used locally — small script + command to reproduce. this fails in both dedicated and local sim with shard-merge enabled.
carla: ```bash
# repro (run from repo root)
python -m tests.long_context_repro \\  --model redwood/llama-7b-int4-v2 \\  --prompt tests/long_docs/legal_10k.txt \\  --max-tokens 8192 \\  --kv-shard-merge merge-on-evict \\  --quant-mode int4
```
carla: clipped output (around token 6512):
carla: ```
EXPECTED: "...the parties shall be held harmless and indemnified."
ACTUAL:   "...the parties shall be held harmess and indemnified."
```
carla: checksum of kvcache pages before eviction: a3f2.., after eviction: a3f4.. — single-byte diff near index 4096.
mina: that looks like a bitflip or an indexing offset, not rope math. did you try disabling shard-merge?
carla: yes — when i set --kv-shard-merge=none the mismatch disappears (but throughput drops). also disabling kv-prefetch (set prefetch=0) makes it go away.
noah: interesting. could be our prefetch coalescing + quant memcpy path. int4 memcpy path was changed in the last driver patch (PR #4123).
shreyas: i'll run a micro-bisect on the memcpy kernel. can you gdb dump the kvcache buffer right after prefetch and before eviction? simple hexdump + sha256 would help.
carla: putting a small instrument in tests/long_context_repro to dump /tmp/kv_dump_{stage}.bin and a sha256 line. pushing in a branch now.
dev-bot: ci/buildkite: tests/long_context_repro — queued (agent: linux-gpu-11)
mina: if it's only happening when prefetch+merge are both on, maybe our merge-on-evict assumes contiguous offsets in bytes but kv pages are packed differently under int4 stride. i can run an isolated kernel test to validate packing semantics.
noah: also add a short test that compares token-level logits before/after prefetch flush (diff top-5). if logits diverge earlier than tokens, that's better signal.
shreyas: noted. i'll start with kernel bisect against PR #4123 and run your hexdumps. planning to run 6-8 bisect steps, will post logs in this thread.
carla: thanks — i attached the failing prompt slice to the branch as tests/data/failing_slice.txt and the two kv dumps (pre/evict) are in my branch. sharing sha256: pre=bf3c... post=bf3d... small delta at byte 4096-4099.
mina: can you also record the rotor/rope phase vectors at that position? if our rotary application is off-by-one when we reconstruct from packed int4, that would explain single-byte drift causing downstream token errors.
carla: good call — added a rope-dump mode to the script. will re-run and upload.
noah: cool. if anyone finds it's a regression from the quant packing change, we should gate the int4 on an extra validation that checks kvcache checksums on startup to avoid silent corruption in prod.
shreyas: agreed. i'll open a quick PR with a validation and add the bisect notes.
carla: thanks team. i'll keep the reproducer minimal and post artifacts here. :thumbsup:
